title: Väinämöinen: Birth and Song
subtitle: A Kalevala episode in Crawford's English rendering

birth.excerpt: Seven hundred years she labored Ere her first-born was delivered.
birth.note: Verbatim English verse translated by John Martin Crawford from Lönnrot's nineteenth-century compilation of oral poetry; not a transcript of one ancient or single oral witness.

narrativeBlocks.title: Seven hundred years in the womb
narrativeBlocks.body: Ilmatar, the air-daughter, floats on the waters and carries her son for centuries — the Kalevala counts it: thirty years, then seven hundred years — until he is born already old, already wise.

narrativeBlocks.title: Born a sage, not a child
narrativeBlocks.body: Vainamoinen is the eternal singer — born not as an infant but as the old, all-knowing sage, the one who will hold the world's songs.

narrativeBlocks.title: The singer's power
narrativeBlocks.body: His gift is not strength but song: in the Kalevala, a rune sung is more powerful than any sword — Vainamoinen's voice can bind enemies, raise islands, calm storms.

narrativeBlocks.title: The land's first shaper
narrativeBlocks.body: He is the one who finds the first seed, builds the first boat, makes the first kantele — the culture-bringer who shapes the land itself with his hands and his singing.

narrativeBlocks.title: A hero of the North
narrativeBlocks.body: The Finnish hero-ideal is different: not a warrior but a wise old singer, whose weapon is the remembered word — the Kalevala built its whole myth around that power.
